title: HTTP Basic Authentication
subtitle: A 401 challenge, then the username and password base64-encoded into an Authorization header and replayed on every request. Step through it and see why base64 is encoding, not encryption.

steps.label: GET /metrics (no credentials)
steps.lede: The client requests a protected resource with no Authorization header. There is no session and no prior login step — Basic starts with the server challenging.
steps.devtools: Open DevTools (F12) → Network, enable Preserve log. On the 401 row read WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Metrics" in Response Headers — that is the challenge that makes the browser pop its native username/password dialog for the realm.

steps.label: Browser prompts for credentials
steps.lede: In response to the challenge the browser shows the native credential dialog naming the realm. The user types their username and password.
steps.devtools: Not a network event — the native dialog is driven by the WWW-Authenticate header. The browser will cache what you enter per realm and reuse it for matching URLs.

steps.label: Retry with Authorization: Basic
steps.lede: The browser retries the exact same URL, now carrying Authorization: Basic base64(username:password). The credential itself — not a token derived from it — is on the wire.
steps.codeTitle: Decode the Basic header (Console or shell)
steps.devtools: In Request Headers read Authorization: Basic …. The part after Basic is base64(user:pass). Decode it with the snippet — one command reverses it, which is the whole point: it is not encryption.

steps.label: GET /metrics/detail (header replayed)
steps.lede: On the next request the browser re-attaches the identical Authorization header automatically. There is no session and no logout — the raw credential is sent on every call.
steps.devtools: Click through several authenticated rows and confirm the identical Authorization: Basic header on each. Over plain HTTP this would expose the password repeatedly — hence Basic must be paired with TLS and HSTS.

steps.label: No logout — credentials cached per realm
steps.lede: Because the browser caches the credential for the realm, there is nothing to invalidate server-side. Closing the browser (or clearing the realm cache) is the only 'logout'.
steps.devtools: There is no Set-Cookie, no token, no session record — so no server-side revocation. A stolen Basic header is as good as the plaintext password until it is rotated. This is why Basic suits machine-to-machine and locked-down internal endpoints, not user sessions.
